items.title: North Korean fake job interview led to $6.3B Binance heist
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/03/north-korean-fake-job-interview-led-to-63b-binance-heist/5307398 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50365755 Points: 392 # Comments: 238
items.content:
'It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident,' exchange says

North Korean cryptocurrency thieves tricked a Binance software engineer into downloading malware onto their work-issued computer during a fake job interview process before last week's record-breaking $6.3 billion heist .

In an incident report published on Tuesday, the cryptocurrency exchange said several techniques - including social engineering via fake job interviews, malware downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint takeover, and an “advanced transaction-authorization method” - led to the October 29 security breach.

“Our current investigation indicates that this was a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign,” the incident report said. “It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident.”

Over the weekend, the FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking operation linked to Lazarus Group , known for combining espionage with massive cryptocurrency heists . The Pyongyang-backed crew is also highly adept at job market scams - both posing as IT workers , who are then hired by Western companies , and as potential employers to lure software engineers into downloading malware and infecting corporate devices .

The attack prep began back in June with a supply chain attack when one of its engineers downloaded a malicious Homebrew installation . While the malware was detected by the security team, the device was replaced, and all affected credentials rotated, “Engineer A’s role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker,” the report says.

Three months later, the social engineering part of the attack happened.

In September, another software engineer was contacted via a “legitimate job-hunting platform” by someone purporting to be a project director who arranged a series of job interviews for the Binance engineer with the fake company. During the first round - a live video interview with the engineer and a fake HR rep - the interviewer “shared a social media account with him, including personal photos and videos posted on the platform, in order to build trust,” according to the report. “This was more advanced and deceptive than previously seen social engineering approaches.”

The second interview with someone purporting to be the CEO of the phony company was conducted on a “popular social chat app,” and toward the end, the CEO instructed the engineer to download an “assignment” containing a malware-laced code repository. The code executed on his work computer during the setup process, which kicked off a series of unauthorized activities.

According to Binance, the malware replaced a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version, which executed commands and established communication with an attacker-controlled external server. The attackers also took steps to hide the malicious script and evade detection, and it worked. Binance’s endpoint security tools did not immediately detect the malware.

RENAME pyenv_ → pyenv (3,414 B) ← replace it with a malicious version

Then, on October 20, the miscreants used the compromised computer and an internal AI tool to gain access to the computers of wallet DevOps engineer A and another wallet software developer, Engineer C.

Engineer A had a container deployment permission token on his computer, which the Norks soon discovered. On October 29, the attacker accessed Engineer C's computer, used the stolen credentials from Engineer A to deploy a container, and triggered a script to launch the cryptocurrency-stealing attack.

As of Tuesday, Binance said it has rebuilt the compromised wallet system and internal AI tool, and replaced all of the affected devices. It also decommissioned all credentials and tokens assigned to the compromised engineers, and is working with law enforcement, blockchain intel firms, and security researchers to trace and freeze the assets.

The crypto exchange has also hired independent cybersecurity experts to conduct a cybersecurity review of the incident, and recommend additional protective measures. Binance said it’s also working to establish a security research fund and initiatives with AI companies and security shops to focus on AI security in blockchain environments.®

items.title: Everything you need to know from the US midterm elections
items.summary: Democrats secured some big wins - and a few historic firsts - earning congratulations from President Trump.
items.content:
Democrats have won both the US Senate and House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.

Projected results have provided the party with a number of things to celebrate - and rival Republicans some reasons to commiserate .

Here is everything you need to know about some of the big Democratic wins and some historic firsts .

Democrats have tallied up victories in states that were comfortably won by Trump two years ago in the presidential election.

With James Talarico winning a seat in the US Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa being elected state governor, Democrats scored two statewide victories in Texas - ending a string of defeats they have endured for almost two generations.

Talarico's supporters went beserk as the projected results arrived at an election-night party, wrote the BBC's Gary O'Donoghue. Attendees hugged, kissed and drank to a reality they dared not believe would come true.

Hinojosa became the first Latina to be elected governor of the state.

Among the other states where history was made by the Democrats were Kansas, where Adam Hamilton took a closely-fought Senate seat - giving the state its first Democratic senator for nearly a century.

REACTION: Trump accepts Democrats did a 'good job' in election

ANALYSIS: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night

Senior party figures who cheered the results included Hakeem Jeffries, the top Democrat in the House of Representatives, who is now poised to take over as the Speaker of the lower chamber of Congress.

"Today begins the great American comeback," he told a crowd of supporters.

If Jeffries' colleagues choose to keep him as the leader of their party's delegation in House, he will be the next Speaker, taking over from Republican Mike Johnson and becoming the first black person to fill that role.

Trump spoke throughout the evening to a number of US media outlets, striking a conciliatory tone and conceding that the Democrats did a "good job" .

He said he would accept the results and that he was looking forward to working with the opposition party - albeit he would still have the power, as president, to veto legislation that Democrats advance through Congress.

Trump distanced himself from some of the Republican candidates who contested the election, saying: "In some cases they didn't like the candidates, and in some cases those candidates were not my friend."

He acknowledged that the US-Israel war on Iran, which has impacted consumer prices in the US, had affected the vote. Trump argued that high fuel prices meant voters could not see how well his economy was doing "as much as they should have", adding: "The gasoline was caused by Iran."

Listen to Americast: Democrats make historic shift in US politics

Abdul El-Sayed has become the first Muslim person elected to the US Senate - after claiming victory in Michigan in what was one of a handful of closely fought contests. His win means the seat stays in Democratic hands.

He defeated Republican opponent Mike Rogers , who received the surprise backing of El-Sayed's Democratic rival in the primary contest, Haley Stevens, who changed her endorsement at the eleventh hour.

The race was one of the bitterest of the midterms. Trump invoked 9/11 and even called El-Sayed a "jihadist" without citing any evidence, prompting a backlash and accusations of Islamophobia.

El-Sayed's supporters went wild when he took the stage to celebrate his claimed victory, wrote the BBC's Nada Tawfik. He said: "Up until right about now, you might have noticed I always say 'inshallah,' or 'God willing,' whenever the outcome of this race was mentioned."

He went on to say: "But today, tonight, we can turn that 'inshallah' into 'alhamdulillah'. For the right-wing ops, that just means 'praise be to God.'"

The defeat of Susan Collins, who has served as the Republican senator for Maine for three decades, was one indicator of the scale of the Republican losses.

She was felled by Democratic candidate Troy Jackson , a logger who sought to point to his background to persuade blue-collar Mainers to vote for him.

In a statement reported by US media, Collins conceded defeat and said it had been the "honour of my life" to serve the state for 30 years.

The BBC's Helena Humphrey described a sombre atmosphere at Collins's watch party in the city of Maine - where the song Closing Time was played.

Collins entered the race as one of the most vulnerable incumbent Republicans seeking re-election, and found that her tactic to distance herself from Trump did not work.

Ashley Hinson suffered the same fate in Iowa, losing that closely-fought Senate seat to Josh Turek. Hinson had slightly distanced herself from the president, urging him to end the war with Iran and breaking with him on easing beef tariffs, while at the same time defending Trump's broader tariff policies as important.

Among the other firsts of the night were in Florida, where Republican Byron Donalds has become the state's first black governor , following a hearty endorsement from Trump.

Donalds, who will take over the job from Ron DeSantis, said his state was the "envy of the nation", and that he would work to make the state more affordable.

The result was one of the few high points of an otherwise difficult evening for the Republicans.

In the neighbouring state of Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former mayor of Atlanta, won the governor's race, becoming the first black governor and first woman to be elected to the state's highest office.

The BBC's Carl Nasman described ecstatic scenes as the race was projected blue. Bottoms defeated Republican Rick Jackson, a billionaire businessman and healthcare executive. The state has also not had a Democratic governor for more than 20 years.

Elsewhere, Democrat Chris Pappas became the first openly gay man elected to the Senate. He celebrated on stage alongside his husband in New Hampshire.

Pappas defeated former Republican Senator John Sununu in the race, whom he thanked on Tuesday, saying: "We all owe John Sununu a big debt of gratitude for his public service for the people of New Hampshire."

In Colorado, Melat Kiros became the first woman elected to Congress from Gen Z - meaning those who were born between 1997 and 2012.

Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here . Those outside the UK can sign up here .

items.title: Mocktastic: A Meshtastic Node on Arduino
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/Vapmuz/Mocktastic Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50365516 Points: 22 # Comments: 1
items.content:
Mocktastic is a small, customizable Meshtastic-compatible LoRa client for ESP32 boards using ArduinoIDE environment. It is an educational and experimental implementation, not a fork of the official Meshtastic firmware. The project demonstrates how to build and decode Meshtastic packets in C++, and includes a working environmental-sensor example.

DECODER provides an interactive serial shell for receiving, decoding, and sending text messages on configured Meshtastic channels and direct messages.

SENSOR turns the board into a DHT22 temperature and humidity sensor. It can send measurements and respond to /dht messages on its configured private channel.

The implementation targets the LilyGO T3 LoRa32 V1.6.1 (ESP32-PICO and SX1276) and is intended to be adapted to other compatible ESP32/LoRa hardware.

The project uses MBDTLS for the cryptographic part during the test phase and Nano-Protobuf as a lightweight protobuf encoder. The tests are written using Doctest’s lightweight C++ tests.

The repository root contains meshtastic_decoder/ , which holds the firmware and host-side tests:

Arduino entry point, board integration, radio setup, and compile-time mode selection.

Cryptographic operations used by the client, including AES and X25519.

Higher-level Meshtastic packet handling, encryption, and Protobuf payloads.

Shell command parsing and high-level message operations; a good starting point when extending the client.

Nanopb runtime and generated Meshtastic Protobuf definitions.

Doctest-based unit tests for the platform-independent logic.

I used Python’s unittest approach as a model for testing individual, predictable units of logic. The project keeps protocol and utility logic separate from hardware effects so it can be exercised on a development machine. The tests themselves are written with the lightweight doctest framework and compile with bundled test dependencies.

The Makefile builds and runs the tests as one step. Tests cover the platform-independent functions, cryptography, Meshtastic packet handling, and shell parsing; changes to radio or sensor behavior should also be checked on the target hardware. To build the API documentation, install Doxygen and Graphviz, then run make doxygen from meshtastic_decoder/ ; the generated documentation is written to meshtastic_decoder/docs/html/ .

You need an ESP32 board and a Semtech SX1276-family LoRa radio. The SENSOR variant also requires a DHT22. The tested board is the LilyGO T3 LoRa32 V1.6.1, which integrates the ESP32 and LoRa radio.

Install Arduino IDE, download or clone this repository, and open meshtastic_decoder/meshtastic_decoder.ino . Install these libraries through the Arduino Library Manager:

open build_opt.h and put your hard-coded filepath. It should result like this: "Hard/coded/path/…​/Mocktastic/meshtastic_decoder/nanopb_meshtastic/src" === LoRa pins

Check your board’s specifications to identify the corresponding pins. The following mapping is for the LilyGO T3 V1.6.1:

Enter the pins for your board in the LoRa pin definitions in meshtastic_decoder/meshtastic_decoder.ino :

Use the following table as a reference for Meshtastic radio presets. Confirm that your selected preset and frequency are supported in your region.

The sketch’s default is EU Medium Fast, configured as follows:

Always verify local radio regulations before transmitting. In the Meshtastic documentation’s Overview page, use Radio Settings and its Frequency Slot Calculator to select a channel and slot and determine the corresponding frequency. Use that frequency in the sketch and make sure it matches the other nodes.

Before compiling, configure PublicChannel , PrivateChannel , Admn , and Device in meshtastic_decoder/keys.h :

For PublicChannel , enter the name and key of the public channel used at the selected frequency. The channel name corresponds to the radio preset (for example, MediumFast ).

For PrivateChannel , enter the name and key of the private channel used for messages.

For Admn , enter the name or node ID and public key of the main node from which you will read messages. Do not put a private key in this entry.

For Device , enter this node’s name, public key, and private key.

Read the channel configuration and node details using the Meshtastic software connected to the relevant node. The Channel structure contains name and key ; Friend contains name and publicKey ; and User contains name , publicKey , and privateKey , in that order. Keys must be hexadecimal strings. Meshtastic may provide them in Base64; convert them to hexadecimal with b64StrToHexStr() before adding them to the configuration.

Use your own credentials and keep private keys and channel keys secret. Do not publish them in a public repository.

The sketch selects its mode at compile time. Near the top of meshtastic_decoder/meshtastic_decoder.ino , keep DECODER defined for the serial shell, or replace it with SENSOR for the DHT22 sensor variant:

Build and upload the sketch with Arduino IDE for your selected ESP32 board.

The DECODER variant is operated over the serial connection. Open the serial monitor at 115200 baud. Its commands are:

For example, send /pub 42 is the answer to write on the public channel. To send hello, world! on the private channel, use /cantine hello, world! .

To enable direct messages with Admn , first send /send_key . This sends this node’s public key so that the official Meshtastic node can establish a private conversation. Then send a direct message with /admn hello, world! .

The SENSOR variant has no interactive shell. It can only be controlled by sending a Meshtastic message on the private channel configured in keys.h . Send /dht on that channel to make the sensor measure temperature and humidity; it sends the result back as a text message on the same channel.

Connect the DHT22 data pin to GPIO 21. A battery is also required for standalone operation.

Keep protocol and parsing logic separate from hardware effects where possible. The portable logic is exercised by host-side tests, while the .ino sketch handles radio, serial, GPIO, and sensor interactions.

For a new shell command, follow the existing pattern in meshtastic_decoder/lora_shell.h and meshtastic_decoder/lora_shell.cpp : add the command to the parser and command enum, then handle it in the dispatcher in meshtastic_decoder/meshtastic_decoder.ino . For higher-level packet operations, start with the functions in lora_shell and the interfaces in meshtastic.h ; use functions.h for lower-level helpers.

Run make test from meshtastic_decoder/ after changing platform-independent logic. Hardware behavior still needs to be verified on the target board and against compatible Meshtastic nodes.

This code is a learning and prototyping project. It has limited field testing, does not provide the reliability or power efficiency of the official Meshtastic firmware, and is not recommended for safety-critical or production use. Its SENSOR battery life, channel handling, and regional radio configuration may need further work for a particular application.

items.title: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat
items.summary: Some Republicans tell the BBC the president's focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost them.
items.content:
Inside the Republican Party, initial shock at the stunning election results on Tuesday night quickly gave way to anger with US President Donald Trump.

After Democrats won upset after upset in deep-red states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina, some Republicans focused their ire on Trump, arguing that his focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost the party control of Congress.

"It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told the BBC. "This is a disaster of the first magnitude. Nobody saw it coming like this."

Most Republicans expected to lose control of the House and were clear-eyed about the challenge of holding onto the Senate in a tough election cycle that favoured the party out of power.

But some said in interviews that Trump dragged them down with unpopular policies, a low job approval rating and obsession over construction projects in Washington.

"It was just one mistake after another," said Gregg Peppin, a Republican strategist in Minnesota. "Clearly, in state after state, people did not like the president's policies."

A White House ally said public disapproval with Trump over the Iran war, tariffs and the administration's immigration crackdown created a "perfect storm" in November.

"There's palpable frustration [within] the party about how this has all played out," the person said, and much of it is directed at Trump. Anger with Trump "is extremely high".

FOLLOW LIVE: Election results and analysis of the US midterms

The BBC spoke to a dozen party operatives, campaign officials, White House allies and others, many of whom spoke on background to offer a candid assessment of Trump's approach to the midterms.

Trump and Republicans had a lot riding on the outcome on Tuesday night. A stronger showing by the president's party - as happened in 2022, when Democrats under then-President Joe Biden lost just nine seats in the House, and gained one in the Senate - would have given Republicans some momentum heading into 2028.

But Trump will instead face a motivated Democratic majority in Congress that is eager to investigate the administration, block his judicial nominees and stymie the rest of his agenda.

The midterms have ushered in an uncertain new phase in Trump's second term and may force Republicans to start grappling with their post-Trump future.

"I don't think his influence is slipping," said Steve Scheffler, the Republican National Committeeman in Iowa, speaking on the eve of the election. Still, he said, when it came to the midterms, "there were things you wish he said differently".

Trump was silent for much of the night before posting a message on Truth Social after the House and Senate were called for Democrats.

"I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter," Trump wrote.

He said in later interviews with the New York Times and Fox News that he would accept the election results. Trump told Fox he was a "little bit surprised" by the election results, but noted that the president's party typically fared poorly in midterm elections.

Since 1934, the party in the White House has only gained seats in three midterm elections. While the Democratic gains in 2026 did not set a record, the party did win dozens of House races, state governor contests and Senate seats, including in states where the party had not been competitive for decades.

Before Tuesday, Democrats had not won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, and had not won a statewide race in Texas in more than three decades. The party also notched surprise upsets in other reliably red states like South Carolina that were thought to be safe seats for Republicans just weeks before Election Day.

Trump and Vice-President JD Vance held dozens of campaign rallies in the run-up to the midterms. The principal Trump-aligned Super PAC, MAGA Inc., spent hundreds of millions backing Republican candidates.

Trump allies said it was unfair to hold him responsible for the party's election losses. They pointed to the history of midterm elections, and said the party was saddled with weak Republican candidates in battleground states like Georgia, Michigan and Texas.

Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate nominee in Texas, ran "the worst Senate campaign in the country from either side of the aisle," said another Texas Republican operative, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. "If Ken's campaign knocked on 100,000 doors I'd be shocked," the source said. The person added that Paxton's victorious Democratic opponent, James Talarico, ran "a really good and smart campaign."

Others defended Trump's autumn campaign schedule, noting that he had to balance his day job of running the country with midterm travel.

"He's the president. He's not going to spend his time campaigning 24/7," said Krish Mathrani, the Michigan Republican Party's youth chair. Mathrani said Trump's campaign rallies helped drive up enthusiasm among Republican voters. "President Trump is a turnout machine," he said.

That's true in presidential elections. But Trump's vaunted turnout operation has failed to deliver in elections when he's not on the ballot, and 2026 proved no different.

Voters rejected Trump's argument that the economy was better on his watch and that he was achieving his aims in the war with Iran. The effort by Trump to portray Democrats as extreme socialists also fell flat, as voters handed victories to moderates like Roy Cooper in North Carolina.

"That just didn't work with Cooper," said a Cooper campaign official. "Trying to tag him as some socialist liberal, that wasn't going to fly."

Trump often seemed disinterested in the midterms over the summer, the period of time when Republicans in Congress shifted their focus to the election.

Trump was consumed by the war with Iran abroad and his construction overhaul of Washington at home. The projects included the under-construction ballroom and a helipad on the South Lawn of the White House, renovations to a local golf course, a proposed memorial arch near Arlington Cemetery and renovations to the Kennedy Center.

Events like a UFC match at the White House on Trump's 80th birthday in June created the impression that the president was more interested in feting himself than winning the midterms, several sources said. Trump also repeatedly downplayed the rising costs of gas and often cast the affordability issue as a Democratic hoax.

Trump turned his full attention to the election in September at the Republican Party's midterm convention. The event was a gamble: Republicans hadn't held a midterm convention in decades, and it was an open question whether voters would tune in.

Trump dominated the convention in Dallas, frustrating Republicans who told the BBC they wanted to highlight the party's midterm candidates.

In his rambling keynote speech, Trump pledged to give $5,000 (£3,700) to anyone who voted for Republicans and raised eyebrows with an endorsement of Paxton which included a lengthy criticism of the candidate's lack of charisma and physical appearance.

"Obviously, that's never helpful," Robin Armstrong, Texas' Republican National Committeeman, said of Trump's critique of Paxton. "You're not going to stop what President Trump says. We just have to kind of live with that."

The convention failed to attract a large television audience, and Democrats were quick to call it a failure. "It backfired for Republicans because nobody paid any attention to it," said Terri Burke, the Texas Democratic Party's executive director.

Trump's penchant for straying off-message continued when he hit the campaign trail in the final weeks before Election Day. He made headlines for praising Ohio Republican Senator John Husted's physique, and drew criticism for calling Abdul El-Sayed a "jihadist" in the Michigan Senate race.

As Trump criss-crossed the country stumping for Republican candidates, the White House contended with controversies in Washington. Katie Zacharia was ousted after just five days as White House press secretary, and Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned as the US ambassador to Greece after reports surfaced that she asked a donor to pay her credit card debt.

Trump also faced a backlash in October for striking a deal to buy Russian diesel. The agreement, which blindsided members of Congress and drew condemnation from some Republicans, came just weeks after Trump signed a sanctions bill aimed at cutting off Russian oil and gas revenue.

Democrats used the deal and other scandals swirling around the White House to make the case for retaking control of Congress. The messaging resonated in the end, as Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress in convincing fashion.

A second White House ally said that the president's political aides projected optimism until the final days of the election, even as it became clear the party was headed to defeat.

Now, as Republicans take stock of the loss, several said they were ready to look ahead to the 2028 election.

"Whether that's JD Vance, or Marco Rubio, or Ted Cruz, we've got a pretty big bench," said Scheffler, the state's RNC member. "It'll be a wide open race."

items.title: Nadal set to join Real Madrid board of directors
items.summary: Tennis great Rafael Nadal is set to join the board of Spanish football giants Real Madrid.
items.content:
Tennis great Rafael Nadal is set to join the board of Spanish football giants Real Madrid.

Nadal won 22 Grand Slam titles, two Olympic gold medals and helped Spain claim five Davis Cups before retiring in 2024 .

Real's members will be asked to approve the 40-year-old's appointment to the board at a meeting later this month.

In a statement announcing the move , external , the club said Nadal was "one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world".

"It is a great source of pride that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a benchmark of Spanish and world sport, will become part of our board of directors and contribute, from this position of responsibility, to the present and future of our club," Real added.

The tennis legend - a boyhood Real fan who holds member's number 67,778 - included a photo of himself as a child in a club kit in his response to the news.

"I want to thank president Florentino Perez and the board for proposing that I join the board of directors of Real Madrid," Nadal said in his post on X , external .

"I have accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn, and a willingness to contribute everything I can."

It is currently unclear as to what responsibilities Nadal would hold on the club's board.

Perez was re-elected to serve a new four-year term as Real president in June, having held the office since 2009.

He swiftly appointed Jose Mourinho to a second spell as head coach, hoping to improve the club's fortunes after they went a second season without a trophy in La Liga, the Champions League or the Copa del Rey.

Real are currently third in the league after 11 games - three points behind defending champions Barcelona.

items.title: Crans-Montana, il padre di Elsa: “Dalla Svizzera una specie di ammissione di colpa”
items.summary: Il governo elvetico rinuncia eccezionalmente al rimborso delle spese mediche per i feriti italiani. Il padre della quindicenne di Biella: “Una buona notizia, potrebbe essere un segnale positivo nella trattativa”
items.content:
La rinuncia della Svizzera al rimborso delle spese mediche per i feriti italiani nell'incendio di Capodanno a Crans-Montana è «assolutamente una buona notizia». E potrebbe rappresentare anche «una specie di ammissione di colpa».

A dirlo, interpellato dall'Ansa, è il padre di Elsa , la quindicenne di Biella rimasta gravemente ferita nel rogo del Constellation, il locale in cui la notte di Capodanno si è consumata la tragedia.

Il governo svizzero ha deciso di rinunciare, a titolo eccezionale, al rimborso delle spese mediche sostenute per curare i feriti italiani. Una decisione che il padre della ragazza interpreta come un segnale importante.

"Nel senso che a me sembra anche una specie di ammissione di colpa per la Svizzera fare questo tipo di azione ammissiva”, spiega.

Una scelta che, secondo il padre di Elsa, potrebbe avere un significato anche sul piano delle trattative in corso. “Secondo me ha un valore importante. Poi magari si ferma tutto lì. Ma, siccome siamo in trattativa, potrebbe essere un segnale positivo”.

La rinuncia al rimborso delle cure, dunque, non è soltanto una buona notizia sul fronte delle spese mediche, ma potrebbe rappresentare un passo avanti nel confronto con le autorità svizzere dopo l'incendio che ha provocato morti e feriti.

"Elsa - spiega il padre - è tornata a scuola , sta dando il massimo ma è chiaramente in una situazione di sali e scendi a livello umorale, e anche in una fase della sua vita molto complessa. I 15 anni, i 16 anni sono sicuramente dei periodi di difficoltà enorme, e lei sta cercando di portare avanti tutto quello che ha da fare, cioè andare a scuola, studiare e divertirsi. E lo sta facendo bene, con tante difficoltà, ma chiaramente lo sta facendo. Non è sicuramente un percorso lineare. Dipende dai giorni, dipende dalle situazioni.

Questo modifica il suo umore, naturalmente. Ma è positiva di natura, diciamo". La studentessa era stata dimessa nel giugno scorso dall'ospedale infantile Regina Margherita di Torino , dove si trovava da aprile. Prima aveva trascorso 58 giorni in terapia intensiva del Centro grandi ustionati del Cto del capoluogo piemontese, dove era arrivata alla fine di febbraio in elicottero, dopo un primo ricovero al Kinderspital di Zurigo.

"Non spaventatevi davanti alle difficoltà della vita, ma affrontate tutto con un sorriso", aveva detto Elsa parlando agli studenti di alcune classi di Biella lo scorso settembre.

items.title: Sharp objects found in Halloween sweets in three European nations
items.summary: Dozens of cases are reported in Austria, Germany and Hungary, including a nine-year-old girl hurting her tongue while eating chocolate containing a pin.
items.content:
Needles and other sharp metal objects have been found in sweets handed out over Halloween in Germany, Austria and Hungary, prompting police to issue warnings to parents to check what their children have been given.

Police in a number of German states have reported cases, from Bavaria in the south-east to Lower Saxony in the north.

A girl aged nine hurt her tongue while eating a chocolate bar in Bremervörde, west of Hamburg. A 5cm-long (2in) pin was then found inside it.

Meanwhile, police in Hungary have launched a criminal investigation after nails, screws and pieces of wire were found in sweets handed out to children who had been trick-or-treating in and around the town of Gyömrő, to the east of Budapest.

The local authority said one young girl had been handed a toffee with a nail inside a chocolate wrapper and that she had fortunately noticed in time and had not swallowed the sweet.

Several cases have also been reported across Austria, where Interior Minister Gerhard Karner condemned the incidents as "cowardly, malicious and in some cases life-threatening".

Police there said investigations were under way in four states, and that a 10-year-old girl had suffered a minor injury to her mouth when she bit into a small chocolate bar in the Amstetten area to the east of Linz.

Lower Austria Governor Johanna Mikl-Leitner said the perpetrators had to feel the full force of the law, adding: "Our children deserve a carefree childhood and we'll continue to ensure that."

German police in the south-eastern state of Bavaria said that, while there had been similar cases reported in the past two years, initial figures this year suggested a significant increase in incidents.

As many as 25 cases involving sweets containing needles, screws or nails have been reported by police in Bavaria.

Police in the Middle Franconia region of western Bavaria have also warned of the risk of copycat actions, after a mother found a needle in her child's chocolate bar and reported it to police.

She later returned to the police to say her child had admitted to inserting the needle.

items.title: Trump deriso sui social, vari meme creati con l'intelligenza artificiale
items.summary: Dalla scopa gigante blu che lo spazza via al video di lui dietro le sbarre
items.content: Donald Trump deriso sui social e 'punito' con la sua stessa arma, vale a dire l'intelligenza artificiale. Dopo la sconfitta dei repubblicani alle midterm, spopolano infatti diversi meme creati con l'IA che deridono il presidente americano. Dalla scopa gigante colorata di blu che lo spazza via, al video che lo mostra in carcere con la tuta arancione dei detenuti mentre lo visitano vari personaggi. Tra questi Melania che gli porta l'hamburger, Barack Obama che gli regala un pezzo di sapone insieme a Joe Biden. I due scoppiano a ridere davanti a lui mentre Trump singhiozza rumorosamente dietro il vetro che lo separa dai visitatori in carcere mentre addenta l'hamburger.

items.title: La Svizzera ha rinunciato a chiedere il pagamento delle cure mediche ricevute nel paese dagli italiani feriti nell’incendio di Crans-Montana
items.content:
La Svizzera ha rinunciato a chiedere all’Italia il pagamento delle cure mediche ricevute nel paese dalle 12 persone italiane ferite nell’ incendio di Crans-Montana , prima che queste proseguissero le cure in Italia. L’incendio si era sviluppato nella notte di Capodanno nel locale Le Constellation, provocando la morte di 41 persone e ferendone 115. Il costo delle cure ammonta a 1,5 milioni di franchi svizzeri, circa 1,6 milioni di euro, e resterà quindi a carico della Svizzera.

La decisione è stata presa dal Consiglio federale, cioè in sostanza dal governo svizzero, che in un comunicato ha detto di aver tenuto conto della portata e delle ripercussioni dell’incendio, e del sostegno fornito dall’Italia (enti italiani avevano partecipato alle operazioni di soccorso e una persona assicurata in Svizzera era stata curata in Italia).

Del pagamento di queste spese si parla da aprile , dopo che un ospedale del canton Vallese, dove si trova Crans-Montana, aveva inviato alle famiglie di tre persone ferite una copia delle fatture per le cure mediche, provocando le proteste del governo italiano, che aveva fin da subito fatto intendere di non voler pagare. Formalmente le cure ricevute in Svizzera da un cittadino dell’Unione Europea dovrebbero essere a carico del paese di residenza del paziente.

items.title: Nuova Audi A2 e-tron, i segreti del motore: come fa a consumare meno
items.summary: La nuova A2 e-tron è l’Audi più efficiente di sempre. Per questo risultato è servito un lavoro specifico sul motore ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Audi ha svelato i dettagli del nuovo motore la A2 e-tron. Lo scopo della casa tedesca era di ottenere risultati molto efficienti. Perciò, sono stati implementati miglioramenti relativi all’elettronica di potenza, al motore elettrico e alla trasmissione che, insieme ad accorgimenti aerodinamici, puntano a ottimizzare al massimo, appunto, l'efficienza globale e ridurre i consumi.

A muovere la A2 e-tron è un motore sincrono a magneti permanenti con codice APP350, installato parallelamente all’asse, che presenta miglioramenti strutturali a rotore e statore. In particolare, rispetto alla versione precedente del propulsore (APP310), lo spessore del rotore è stato ridotto di oltre il 30%. Questa misura riduce le perdite nel ferro, che si verificano quando il materiale viene ripetutamente rimagnetizzato.

Inoltre, Audi ha ridisegnato i segmenti del rotore, che non sono più disposti linearmente ma con uno schema sfalsato. Questo intervento ha come conseguenza diretta una drastica riduzione delle vibrazioni (soprattutto nelle partenze da fermo), che si traduce in un abitacolo più silenzioso. Cambia anche la configurazione dell’avvolgimento dello statore, che passa da stella a triangolo. Ciò comporta una riduzione dei rami paralleli e, di conseguenza, una maggiore efficienza dei circuiti in situazioni di utilizzo ordinario, specie nel traffico cittadino.

L'inverter, cuore dell'elettronica di potenza che converte la corrente continua della batteria in corrente alternata per il motore, compie un salto generazionale. Audi ha infatti abbandonato i tradizionali transistor in silicio in favore di nuovi elementi MOSFET in carburo di silicio (SiC). Grazie alle proprietà fisiche di questo materiale, le perdite in fase di commutazione si riducono drasticamente, permettendo al sistema di superare il 97% di efficienza.

A questo si aggiunge un software di gestione adattivo che modula la frequenza di commutazione in base allo stile di guida, ottimizzando ulteriormente i consumi alle velocità medie e nel traffico cittadino.

La corsa all’efficienza di Audi è accelerata dalla nuova trasmissione, più compatta e leggera grazie a interventi tecnici quali l’adozione di rapporti dedicati ai diversi tagli di potenza disponibili in gamma. Nel dettaglio, le versioni da 125 kW e 140 kW hanno un rapporto i=10,21 (significa che per per far compiere alle ruote un giro completo, il motore deve effettuare 10,21 giri), mentre la configurazione da 170 kW ha un rapporto i=11,53. Secondo Audi, questi valori sono studiati per mantenere i regimi del propulsore negli intervalli più efficienti consentiti da materiali e configurazioni, ottimizzando al massimo i consumi.

L’attenzione degli ingegneri si è concentrata anche sulla rugosità delle superfici: sui fianchi dei denti della trasmissione è stata ridotta al minimo per limitare le perdite dovute all’attrito. Questo dettaglio di progettazione ha portato Audi a equipaggiare il gruppo con un olio a bassissima viscosità sviluppato ad hoc, che agevola i passaggi nella trasmissione e riduce significativamente le perdite per sbattimento tra gli ingranaggi.

L'esito di questa ingegnerizzazione è tangibile soprattutto nella versione da 140 kW con pacchetto Efficiency opzionale (che include soluzioni aerodinamiche e di assetto progettate per massimizzare l’autonomia). In questa configurazione, la vettura registra un consumo combinato di appena 12,8 kWh/100 km nel ciclo WLTP.

items.title: Qualche grafico per capire meglio il risultato delle elezioni negli Stati Uniti
items.summary: Dove e di quanto hanno vinto i Democratici? Quali posti si sono spostati più a sinistra? Dov'è che i Repubblicani hanno retto?
items.content:
La portata della vittoria dei Democratici alle elezioni di metà mandato si capisce molto bene guardando dati e mappe sul voto di martedì. Mostrano che i Democratici hanno stravinto un po’ ovunque, e come sono cambiate le cose rispetto alle ultime elezioni, quelle che nel 2024 avevano eletto Donald Trump alla presidenza degli Stati Uniti.

Prima di queste elezioni i Democratici non controllavano né la Camera né il Senato. Martedì sono riusciti a ottenere il controllo di entrambi. Alla Camera si votava per rinnovare tutti e 435 i seggi, al Senato circa un terzo (per la precisione 35 su 100). Via via che procede lo scrutinio il numero dei seggi si sta assestando, ma grossomodo sarà questo.

Alla Camera i Democratici hanno ampiamente superato i 218 seggi necessari per la maggioranza, e ce ne sono ancora decine da assegnare. La maggioranza è quindi già sicura: manca solo capire quanto sarà ampia. Che i Democratici potessero ottenere la maggioranza della Camera era uno scenario dato come molto probabile dai sondaggi, sebbene fossero stati un po’ più cauti sulla dimensione della vittoria.

Meno probabile era che i Democratici riuscissero a prendersi anche il Senato, dove sono arrivati a 54 seggi, sopra i 51 necessari per averne il controllo. I Repubblicani si sono fermati a 44 senatori. Mancano i seggi di Alaska e Mississippi, per cui servirà ancora un po’ di tempo per sapere a chi andranno: ma se anche entrambi andassero ai Repubblicani, i Democratici hanno comunque ottenuto un risultato che nelle previsioni della vigilia era ritenuto ottimistico.

Dei 35 seggi per cui si è votato al Senato, 20 sono stati vinti dai Democratici, e appena 13 dai Repubblicani: questo rende ancora più netto il risultato dei Democratici (oltre che più duraturo: i senatori restano in carica per 6 anni).

Come si vede dal grafico qui sotto, al Senato i Democratici hanno ottenuto diversi seggi che prima erano dei Repubblicani, in stati anche storicamente molto conservatori. Sono quelli indicati con il motivo a righe blu. Al contrario i Repubblicani non sono riusciti a togliere nessun seggio ai Democratici.

Il caso che meglio riassume la portata di questa sconfitta dei Repubblicani è quello del Texas , dove i Repubblicani governavano da decenni; ma ci sono anche il Kansas, dove un candidato Democratico non vinceva dal 1932, e il South Carolina, che è uno stato tradizionalmente molto conservatore.

In Texas i Democratici sono riusciti a conquistare anche diversi seggi che appartenevano ai Repubblicani alla Camera, come si vede dal grafico. Neanche alla Camera i Repubblicani sono riusciti a sottrarre seggi ai Democratici.

I dati fin qui mostrano i risultati per seggi, ma è utile scendere a un maggiore livello di dettaglio così da capire come hanno votato i diversi stati. Il grafico qui sotto mostra i voti per singola contea alla Camera, con le bolle che sono proporzionali al numero di voti conteggiati. Le contee sono divisioni amministrative più piccole dei distretti, che invece sono la parte di territorio che elegge il singolo deputato.

Questo grafico con le frecce invece mostra quale partito ha guadagnato voti rispetto al 2024, nei seggi dove lo scrutinio è concluso. La lunghezza della freccia indica la dimensione del ribaltamento dei voti. Le frecce sono lunghe e fitte soprattutto a Est o Sud-est (in Georgia, North e South Carolina, Mississippi, Louisiana). Gli stati che mancano sono quelli in cui i conteggi sono ancora in corso.

Le poche frecce rosse sono in Illinois, Minnesota e Florida.

In 36 stati si votava anche per il governatore. Come si vede dalla mappa qui sotto sono stati finora cinque i candidati Democratici che hanno sottratto il governo locale ai Repubblicani: è successo in Iowa, Ohio, Georgia, Nevada e Texas, tutti stati in cui Trump aveva vinto alle presidenziali del 2024.

items.title: C’è un accordo per alzare il salario minimo nel settore tessile in Bangladesh, secondo produttore di abbigliamento al mondo
items.content:
In Bangladesh c’è un accordo per innalzare il salario minimo degli oltre quattro milioni di persone che lavorano nel settore tessile: il Bangladesh è il secondo produttore di capi d’abbigliamento al mondo dopo la Cina, e da sabato nel settore c’erano grandi proteste proprio contro i salari, ritenuti inadeguati ai carichi di lavoro. Le proteste hanno portato a scontri, blocchi di strade e autostrade e alla sospensione delle attività in alcune fabbriche, e dunque a conseguenze dirette sulla filiera.

Non si sa ancora di quanto sarà l’aumento: l’accordo è stato annunciato da Babul Akter, che rappresenta i lavoratori in un comitato istituito in questi giorni per discutere il tema, e si sa che entrerà in vigore da gennaio. I lavoratori chiedevano di aumentare il salario minimo mensile da 12.500 mila taka (circa 90 euro) a 30mila (circa 215).

In Bangladesh ci sono migliaia di fabbriche tessili che producono vestiti anche per marchi molto conosciuti, come H&M, Zara o Levi’s, e il settore genera circa quattro quinti delle entrate economiche legate alle esportazioni. Ciononostante chi è impiegato nell’industria tessile ha stipendi bassi e molto spesso condizioni di lavoro pessime. L’aumento più recente, quello che aveva portato il salario minimo a 12.500 taka, era stato deciso tre anni fa , sempre a seguito di grosse proteste.

items.title: Posti improbabili dove hanno votato gli statunitensi
items.summary: Dalla Stazione spaziale internazionale a un centro di cultura iraniana; in chiese e supermercati, circondati da urne funerarie o da procioni
items.content:
Alle elezioni di metà mandato di martedì erano aperti seggi anche in posti strani, come avviene del resto a ogni giro di elezioni negli Stati Uniti. Il senso è aumentare la partecipazione e la capillarità dei seggi, in modo che gli elettori ne abbiano uno per quanto possibile vicino a loro e facile da raggiungere. Nel tempo questo ha incentivato una certa creatività da parte dei funzionari statali, che sono quelli che chiedono ad attività e centri locali se sono disponibili a ospitare un seggio.

Caserme, chiese e lavanderie sono un classico delle raccolte delle agenzie fotografiche. A queste elezioni, tra gli altri, ha votato pure un astronauta dalla Stazione spaziale internazionale. Martedì erano aperti seggi allo zoo, in concessionarie di auto, in un centro di cultura iraniana di Los Angeles e in un parco naturale dell’Iowa intitolato ai procioni.

Nella gallery trovate anche un seggio in un edificio di San Francisco che ospita urne funerarie, e a Chicago in un negozio di abiti e accessori per feste di quinceañera , la tradizione latinoamericana delle feste per le ragazze di 15 anni.

items.title: AI is forcing us to pay off 40 years of technical debt
items.summary: Article URL: https://spectrum.ieee.org/ai-in-cybersecurity-php2shell-vulnerability Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50364336 Points: 749 # Comments: 464
items.content:
Dina Genkina is the computing and hardware editor at IEEE Spectrum

In late October, a slew of major cybersecurity issues came to light. But none were bigger than the so-called PHP2Shell vulnerability , which put a plethora of websites, including those of NASA , Wikipedia , the White House, and all other sites that run on Wordpress or Drupal (among others) at risk of exploits capable of both reading sensitive data and running malicious code on the host server.

As far as anyone is aware, disaster has been averted: The hack was discovered by cybersecurity researchers who reported it to the PHP Foundation, and a patch was released before any bad actors got their hands on the exploit. However, PHP2Shell may be the canary in the coal mine, serving as a warning sign for what’s to come in the age of AI.

“One of the things we’re witnessing now is that all the legacy software that was written by humans over the last 40 years is being exposed,” says Matt Suiche , AI security research lead at the cybersecurity startup Tolmo . “Now it is time for the technical debt to be paid off.”

PHP, which originally stood for “personal home page,” is a programming language created back in 1994 and largely used by legacy sites. The bug underlying the PHP2Shell vulnerability was reported to the PHP Foundation as far back as 2024. The bug caused a common type of issue called an out-of-memory error, in which the amount of memory allocated to a piece of data is too small to hold the data. Normally, this type of error causes the program to crash—an unpleasant but not inherently dangerous result. And so the bug remained unaddressed.

“If you look at any at any point of time, there will be a bunch of bug reports that are waiting to be fixed, which are just crashes. Most people don’t take them very seriously,” says Suman Jana , an associate professor of computer science at Columbia University .

“It’s just that it’s a lot of very specific reasoning that is painful to do. And AI, I think, has done a very good job at that.” –Suman Jana, Columbia University

Earlier this year, the cybersecurity firm Calif offered to independently audit PHP, sponsored by OpenAI . Within two weeks, a researcher at Calif, aided by AI tools, found a way to use the out-of-memory bug to run arbitrary code on the host server, allowing a malicious actor to install malware or read critical data. Now, it was no longer a minor bug—it was a critical vulnerability, and the Calif team alerted the PHP foundation to start working on a patch immediately.

Jana says actually exploiting the bug requires carefully working out a way to jump to a specific point in the memory for a particular program running on the server, and work out exactly which bits to overwrite in what order to gain control of the system. “It’s not really rocket science,” he says. “It’s just that it’s a lot of very specific reasoning that is painful to do. And AI, I think, has done a very good job at that.”

To be clear, the researchers at Calif (as well as OpenAI and Wiz, a cybersecurity company that confirmed and expanded the vulnerabilities) had deep knowledge of both cybersecurity and the PHP language. “I’m not claiming that AI can do it all by itself. It clearly cannot,” Jana says. “But it is improving a lot, so the top 0.1 percent [of experts] can get a lot more stuff done, and also just below the 0.1 percent now will be able to go there without understanding all the nitty-gritty details.”

After the exploits were disclosed to the PHP Foundation, a team of four engineers spent two months developing a patch to release as quickly as possible.

“There is a fundamental asymmetry in finding bugs and fixing bugs,” Jana says. “Because when you’re fixing bugs you have to make sure that you know all parts of that attack are closed, and also that you don’t break any existing functionality.”

This asymmetry puts a lot of strain on the defenders, especially for open-source software such as PHP. Maintaining open-source projects that don’t have clear revenue streams despite being widely used is a long-standing challenge that precedes AI hacking tools. But those tools make the issue more pressing than ever.

One way to stay ahead of such issues going forward is to empower the defenders with more money and access to frontier cybersecurity AI models . “These frontier labs are donating some of their token budgets to look into these bugs, which I think is great,” Jana says. “I think that should happen more, either through some concerted effort or through donations.”

Jana is also optimistic that formal verification tools to automate the patching side of the equation are also advancing quickly, including a new release from Anthropic on 22 October. “The patch is LLM-generated, and then an LLM generates the proof that the patch is correct,” says Jana. “The only thing not done by an LLM is the proof checker, because somebody has to check the proof, because LLMs hallucinate. So, you want something that is formal.”

Hopefully, the combination of specialized AI models and formal verification tools will make patching vulnerabilities nearly as automatable as finding them.

Matthew Green , an associate professor of computer science at Johns Hopkins University Information Security Institute, is less optimistic. “Nobody’s going to fix this problem until something really bad happens,” he says. “And PHP2Shell wasn’t bad enough to be really bad. So when something really bad happens, which is going to be maybe sometime in early 2027, something bad that normal people are upset by, then suddenly people will start doing this. We’re going to fund everything.”

In the meantime, Green says, update your software. “If your phone is like, ‘Hey, there’s a security update available, do you want to install it,’ don’t wait till next week. Just do it.”

One thing’s for sure—PHP2Shell is just the beginning. “This won’t be the last one for sure,” Jana says. “It’s just who finds it. Hopefully, the white-hat hackers find it first, like this one.”

Dina Genkina is an associate editor at IEEE Spectrum focused on computing and hardware. She holds a PhD in atomic physics and lives in Brooklyn.

items.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
items.summary: As South Africans vote in local elections, residents tell the BBC they are tired of the poor quality of services they get.
items.content:
South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC).

This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes.

Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations.

Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection.

For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended.

Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime.

At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election. Two decades later its share dropped to 40%.

Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral.

"What I'm seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers," he told supporters at the party's final election rally on Sunday.

In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support.

The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views. One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard.

We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner. Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so.

They cited a lack of change and deteriorating delivery of basic services.

But Ntombela was looking forward to voting for the first time and thought it might lead to change.

"We face many challenges in Alexandra. There's rubbish everywhere and we struggle with electricity and water and many other issues," he said.

Just metres away, heaps of rubbish lay gathered beneath a streetlight pole covered in election posters from the different political parties.

On the other side of the street, drain water trickles through the many potholes that have gutted that part of the road.

The BBC also spoke to Zandile Mncube, who said she wouldn't vote, even though she is registered to do so.

The 33-year-old woman also cited poor service delivery and performance by local leaders for her decision.

"It makes no difference [whether I vote or not]. Things have gotten worse over the years," she said.

Alex, as the township is known, is a stone's throw away from Sandton, Africa's richest square mile, but the differences could not be starker.

Sandton is known for its skyscrapers, designer shops and well-maintained roads but in Alex, houses are sandwiched together and rubbish, either piled together or left strewn across the pavement, is everywhere. The stench of raw sewage and uncollected rubbish is heavy in the air, but residents appear used to it.

The issues plaguing Alexandra are not unique. A drive around Gauteng province reveals similar patterns of neglect and disrepair, especially in the townships.

South of Johannesburg, Soweto looks marginally cleaner than Alexandra, but residents also complain about service delivery.

Mduduzi Makhubo, 45, has lived in Soweto his entire life and he told the BBC of the community's daily struggles with accessing water and electricity.

"Every Monday we know we won't have water after 2pm," he said.

Makhubo is registered to vote and intends to use his vote to deal with the "arrogance" he says local leaders have towards residents and "change the status quo".

Can this man broaden the appeal of a South African party seen by some as 'too white'?

South Africa's political marriage of convenience avoids divorce - just

These areas offer a small, but important, glimpse into the state of South Africa's local governance.

Years of reports by the auditor-general have highlighted the dire state of most of South Africa's 257 municipalities.

A recent report only gave 39 clean audits - the highest ranking a public entity can achieve - between 2024 and 2025. None of Gauteng's three metro cities, Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, featured in this list.

Earlier this year auditor-general Tsakani Maluleke said Johannesburg "needs ongoing attention".

"If we don't that, we are going to continue on this slide where financial health deteriorates [and] where service delivery continues to be compromised, which is what we are living," she told lawmakers.

The city has been labelled "effectively bankrupt" due to the dire state of its finances. Dirty streets, unstable electricity supply and persistent water issues have been common for years.

Experts the BBC spoke to agreed that all eyes will be on Africa's wealthiest city as well as the country's seven other biggest municipalities, or metros, particularly those in Gauteng when the results come in.

Of South Africa's eight metros, only three are governed by a single party. In Gauteng, all three metros are governed by coalition governments, with the ANC the largest party.

Political analyst Melanie Verwoerd said the elections would be a "verdict ... and judgment" on the ANC.

"And the expectation is that the ANC generally in the country is going to [perform] the worst it's ever done," she said.

Several polls point to a continued decline in support for the party in Wednesday's election, contested by over 500 political parties.

One, conducted by Ipsos, put the ANC's support at 30%, down from the 46% it got at the last local elections in 2021.

The same poll, along with others, points to a slight increase in electoral support for the Democratic Alliance (DA), especially in Johannesburg. Ipsos predicts the DA will garner 25% support in this election, up from 22% last time.

DA leader Helen Zille has been vying for the mayoral chain in the city and her unusual campaign has attracted a lot of attention.

The former Cape Town mayor has been captured swimming in crater-sized potholes, ziplining over sinkholes and riding into her final rally in the city in a classic BMW 325i, known locally as a "Gusheshe".

She believes the DA is the country's best choice for a government, telling local radio broadcaster 702 last week that "towns and cities that work best are under DA governance".

Verwoerd, a former ANC MP and South Africa's ambassador to Ireland, predicted that coalitions would continue being the order of the day across Gauteng.

These types of arrangements have often been viewed as unstable and chaotic at a local level and the constant change in leadership, usually caused by parties falling out with each other, has affected service delivery in many municipalities.

Verwoerd said in her view, the most stable coalitions would be those that replicate what the ANC and DA have done on a national level, where the historic rivals have agreed to share power.

Reflecting on Cape Town, she said it was unlikely that the DA would lose control of the municipality. The coastal city is widely considered the country's best-performing metro and has been run by the DA since the late 2000s when it unseated the ANC.

Ethekwini, which includes the port city of Durban in KwaZulu-Natal, would be a "different story", Verwoerd said.

The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has been projected to perform well in the area but it is unclear if it will secure the outright majority needed to run the metro. Polls suggest it won't and will need partners to form a government.

The party was founded by former South African President Jacob Zuma and was the biggest party across his home province of KwaZulu-Natal in the 2024 provincial election.

Verwoerd reflected that while various options were on the table for the party, forming a government would be "very messy" given its refusal to work with either the ANC or DA.

A confident Zuma, addressing supporters on Sunday, vowed to take control of a number of municipalities after the elections.

Another political analyst Dr Levy Ndou echoed Verwoerd's assessment, saying that a coalition between the DA and ANC seemed unavoidable in most metros.

"We're not sure whether the arrangement of the government of national unity could have the potential to influence how the metros are going to be run," he said.

Both experts also spoke about the declining voter turnout in South Africa's elections. Over 29 million citizens are registered to vote, but the turnout, especially among young people, has seen a steady decline.

Ndou attributed this to the "calibre" of the candidates campaigning and the lack of visibility of local councillors, who are often the ones elected to lead their neighbourhoods, in election campaigns.

items.title: Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
items.summary: The US imposed sanctions on Rwanda's army over its role in the conflict in DR Congo.
items.content:
The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March.

The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL).

However this is the first time the NBA has revealed the reasons behind the APR's removal.

The association was responding to complaints by two US senators, who sent a letter asking them to reconsider their partnership with the Rwandan team. The US placed sanctions on the Rwandan army, accusing it of fuelling the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo in March.

The senators said the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights".

Last week, the US also imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its support for the M23 rebel group which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo. Rwanda denies backing the rebels despite overwhelming evidence.

Rwanda is an official BAL partner and pays the league to host its finals at the 10,000-seat BK Arena in the capital, Kigali.

The evidence that shows Rwanda is backing rebels in DR Congo

In the letter to the NBA dated 23 October, Democratic Senator Jeffrey Merkley and Republican counterpart Marsha Blackburn gave the association until 2 November to give a written response regarding its continued partnership with Rwanda.

"What is the NBA red line for accepting money from foreign governments that commit human rights abuses?" the senators asked.

Among other queries, they also questioned how the association could "reconcile its continued partnership with Rwanda with its purported commitment to justice".

In its response, NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the Rwandan team "had been withdrawn" from the BAL following the sanctions imposed earlier in the year, American sports website ESPN reports.

The NBA said the APR basketball club would remain barred while the US sanctions are in place.

The APR is one of Rwanda's top basketball teams and represented the country in the BAL in 2024 and 2025, when it came third. It was replaced by the RSSB Tigers this year.

The BAL is a pan-African basketball league established and co-organised by the NBA and the basketball's world governing body Fiba.

It is a professional league featuring 12 club teams from across the continent.

Rwanda has hosted all but one of the league's final and playoff matches since the inaugural match in 2021.

The NBA reportedly receives millions of dollars annually from the country for the marketing and partnership rights.

DR Congo has repeatedly condemned Rwanda's high-profile international sports deals, including with the NBA, European football clubs and Formula 1, asking them to end their campaigns.

It argues that these help Rwanda clean up its global image, while the conflict continues in eastern DR Congo.

items.title: È ripartita la nave da crociera di lusso che si era fermata in Cambogia a causa dei prezzi del carburante, ma senza i passeggeri
items.content:
Nella notte tra martedì e mercoledì la nave da crociera di lusso Villa Vie Odyssey è ripartita dalla Cambogia, dopo essere rimasta ferma per quasi una settimana al porto di Sihanoukville, nel sud del paese, a causa degli alti costi del carburante . Sulla nave c’erano circa duecento persone che avevano comprato o affittato cabine per vivere viaggiando intorno al mondo: tutte erano state obbligate a sbarcare in Cambogia, e la nave è ripartita solo con una cinquantina di membri dell’equipaggio (che prima ne aveva 150).

La Villa Vie Odyssey è una delle due navi per crociere “infinite” attualmente operative: ospita fino a 650 passeggeri, che possono affittare una cabina a partire da 3.500 dollari al mese (circa 3mila euro) o per tutta la durata del viaggio, pagando una cifra dai 120mila ai 440mila dollari (dai 100mila ai 400mila euro suppergiù). Era partita nel 2024 da Belfast, nell’Irlanda del Nord, e contava di restare in viaggio per anni: non è chiaro dove sia diretta adesso.

items.title: Netflix ti consiglierà le cose da vedere con l’IA: lanciato AI Discover
items.summary: Un’IA che impara dai gusti dell’utente le serie e i film che potrebbero piacergli, mostrandoli per tema. In distribuzione negli USA ma in ampliamento ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Netflix sta sperimentando un sistema di suggerimento dei contenuti da vedere potenziato dall’IA. La nuova scheda dell’app per smart TV si chiama infatti “AI Discover” .

Grazie a ciò che gli utenti hanno messo nelle loro liste di visione e le reazioni con i pollici rispetto a quanto visto, Netflix ha detto di avere imparato nel corso degli anni ciò che può piacere agli utenti e ha trasferito questa sua conoscenza alla IA che intende proporre cose nuove da vedere.

AI Discover parte proprio da consigli tematici, per esempio mostrando sotto diverse etichette come “Saghe famigliari” o “Intrighi di corte”, ma anche “Spaventami” e “Film per una serata in famiglia”, un carosello di film e serie tv che ritiene adatti all’utente.

Scegliendo un tema si amplia l’offerta dei contenuti associabili a esso , che si può cambiare con “Mostrami qualcosa di diverso” per avere altre proposte affini.

Per ora AI Discover è in distribuzione agli utenti negli Stati Uniti che usano Netflix in inglese, ma ha previsto di allargare la platea nel corso delle prossime settimane. Non sappiamo se e quando arriverà anche in Italia, però esiste già una pagina di supporto tradotta nella nostra lingua che chiama la funzione “Area IA”.

items.title: Il presidente Herzog accetta i risultati ufficiali delle elezioni
items.summary: 'L'inizio delle consultazioni nel giorno simbolico dell'uccisione di Rabin'. Il giudice Solberg, presidente della Commissione elettorale: 'Voci cercano di minare il risultato elettorale'
items.content:
"Ricevo i risultati ufficiali delle elezioni e li approvo secondo la legge. Ho piena fiducia nelle indagini dello Shin Bet e della polizia: ogni sospetto di influenza estera va investigato . Ci vuole pazienza fino alla fine delle indagini. Ho piena fiducia nello Shin Bet e nella procuratrice generale e so che collaboreranno", ha dichiarato il presidente Herzog dopo aver ricevuto i risultati ufficiali delle elezioni.

"Inizio le consultazioni in un giorno simbolico, il 4 novembre, la data in cui fu ucciso il primo ministro Itzhak Rabin 31 anni fa. Per sempre questa data sarà un ricordo duro, un avvertimento di cosa può accaderci quando le divergenze si trasformano in odio, quando la rivalità politica sfocia nella violenza. Non c'è posto per la violenza tra noi, non fisica né verbale, non contro persone singole né contro interi settori della società", ha aggiunto Herzog.

"Ci sono voci che cercano di minare i risultati elettorali, e questo rappresenta un pericolo reale", ha affermato il giudice Solberg, presidente della Commissione elettorale, parlando al fianco del presidente Herzog. "Ciò compromette la possibilità di un cambio di governo pacifico. Reagiremo a una situazione in cui 'tutti i partiti sono vincitori'. Siamo tenuti a rispettare le regole democratiche del gioco. Dobbiamo riconoscere la decisione degli elettori e agire di conseguenza. Non dobbiamo deviare da questa strada che è alla base della nostra forza. Sono emersi seri sospetti, e saremo tenuti ad affrontarli. Tutte le parti stanno lavorando per accertare la verità, non è possibile andare oltre", ha aggiunto.

items.title: Il supporto per TV è un mobile con due cassetti e le ruote. Le novità di Techly
items.summary: Le novità coprono televisori fino a 75 pollici e spaziano dai supporti da pavimento con elementi d’arredo integrati alle staffe full-motion per il montaggio a parete ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Techly ha annunciato nuovi supporti per TV e monitor con quattro nuovi modelli che comprendono soluzioni da pavimento con mobile o cassetti integrati e una staffa a parete orientabile per televisori fino a 75 pollici.

Tra le novità c’è un supporto mobile da pavimento bianco con mobile color legno chiaro, compatibile con TV da 32 a 65 pollici. È regolabile in altezza da 1.173 a 1.383 mm e il mobile è largo 55 cm. Costa 159,52 euro.

Ma è la variante a essere più curiosa. Mantiene un’impostazione simile, ma aggiunge dei cassetti con maniglia, utili per riporre oggetti di vario genere, dai telecomandi alle console portatili e quindi non lasciarli esposti. Le dimensioni sono più compatte: è largo 42 cm. In questo caso la compatibilità dichiarata va da 32 a 60 pollici. Il supporto VESA resta lo stesso (massimo 400 x 400) e supporta fino a 40 kg. Il prezzo in questo caso è di 138,99 euro.

Nella gamma di supporto per TV e monitor, Techly ha introdotto anche un supporto mobile da pavimento senza mobile integrato, compatibile con TV da 32 a 75 pollici. La caratteristica principale è la possibilità di regolare l’altezza dello schermo: ci sono quattro regolazioni, da 817 mm a 1.042 mm.

Può essere utile, per esempio, quando il pannello non viene utilizzato sempre dalla stessa posizione oppure quando si vuole evitare un’installazione permanente a parete. La base prevede quattro ruote per gli spostamenti. Il supporto VESA arriva a 600 x 400 e supporta fino a 50 kg. Costa 115 euro.

La quarta novità è più canonica: una staffa full-motion destinata al montaggio a muro, anch’essa compatibile con televisori da 32 a 75 pollici. Può essere inclinata da +5° a -12° e ruotata da +90° a -90°.

Inoltre, è integrata una bolla di livello per agevolare il montaggio del TV. Anche in questo caso il supporto VESA arriva a 600 x 400 ma può sostenere finoa 45 kg.

Dei quattro modelli è ampiamente la soluzione più economica: costa 39,60 euro.
